subject: maths

concepts.title: Count of Multiples up to a Limit
concepts.definition: The quantity of positive multiples of a given number that do not exceed a chosen maximum value.
concepts.key_idea: Integer division of the upper limit by the divisor gives the exact count of multiples.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: find how many multiples of {number} lie up to {limit}
calculate how many times a multiple of {number} occurs from 1 to {limit}
what is the total count of multiples of {number} less than or equal to {limit}
how many numbers up to {limit} are divisible by {number}
determine the frequency of multiples of {number} within 1 and {limit}

solution_steps.explain: Perform integer division of the upper limit by the divisor number.
Confirm that integer division is valid since multiples occur at regular intervals of the divisor.
The quotient from the division is the exact count of multiples of the number up to the limit.

concepts.title: Nth Common Multiple
concepts.definition: The nth term in the ordered sequence of common multiples shared by two or more numbers.
concepts.key_idea: Every common multiple of a set of numbers is an integer multiple of their lowest common multiple.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: find the {n}th common multiple of numbers with LCM {lcm}
calculate the {n}th occurrence of a common multiple given least common multiple {lcm}
at what number is idli-vada said for the {n}th time if first occurrence is {lcm}
what is the {n}th multiple shared by two numbers whose LCM is {lcm}
determine the value of the {n}th common multiple for LCM {lcm}

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the position n by the least common multiple to obtain the nth common multiple.

solution_steps.action: verify n is a positive integer
solution_steps.explain: Confirm the position n is valid since common multiples occur at every multiple of the LCM.
The product gives the exact value at which both numbers share their nth common multiple.

concepts.title: Common Factors and Shared Divisors
concepts.definition: Numbers that divide two or more given integers completely without leaving any remainder.
concepts.key_idea: Shared factors represent common exact divisors or valid stepping distances for both numbers.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: find the common factors of {num1} and {num2}
what jump sizes can land on both {num1} and {num2}
calculate all numbers that divide both {num1} and {num2} exactly
determine shared factors for the pair {num1} and {num2}
which jump sizes reach both treasures placed at {num1} and {num2}

solution_steps.explain: Find all positive integers dividing num1 without remainder.
Find all positive integers dividing num2 without remainder.
Extract the integers that appear in both factor lists.

concepts.title: Perfect Numbers
concepts.definition: A positive integer for which the sum of all its factors equals twice the number itself.
concepts.key_idea: Adding all positive divisors of a perfect number results in exactly double its value.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: verify if {num} is a perfect number
check whether sum of factors of {num} equals twice {num}
find if {num} satisfies the condition of a perfect number
determine if {num} is perfect by summing its factors
is {num} a perfect number between 1 and 10

solution_steps.explain: List all positive integers that divide the given number.
Add all factors together.
Check if the sum of factors equals twice the given number.

concepts.title: Prime and Composite Numbers
concepts.definition: Natural numbers greater than 1 with exactly two distinct factors are prime, while those with more than two factors are composite.
concepts.key_idea: Primes have no divisors other than 1 and themselves, whereas composites can form non-trivial rectangular arrangements.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: classify {num} as prime or composite
which of the following numbers are prime: {num1}, {num2}, {num3}
determine whether {num} is a prime number
identify if {num} has more than two factors
find how many factors {num} has to check if it is prime

solution_steps.explain: Determine all positive integers that divide the given number.
If factor count is exactly 2, it is prime; if greater than 2, it is composite.
State whether the number is prime or composite based on the factor count found.

concepts.title: Twin Primes
concepts.definition: Pairs of prime numbers that have a numerical difference of two.
concepts.key_idea: Twin primes are consecutive odd prime numbers separated by a single even composite number.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: find twin prime pairs between {start} and {end}
determine if {p1} and {p2} are twin primes
check whether primes {p1} and {p2} differ by 2
identify twin prime pairs less than {limit}
are {p1} and {p2} twin primes

solution_steps.explain: Ensure both numbers in the pair are prime numbers.
Subtract the smaller prime from the larger prime and verify if the difference is 2.
If both numbers are prime and differ by exactly 2, the pair is a twin prime; otherwise it is not.

concepts.title: Co-prime Numbers
concepts.definition: Two numbers that share no common factor other than 1.
concepts.key_idea: Co-prime pairs have 1 as their sole shared divisor, meaning no larger common step size exists.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: check if {num1} and {num2} are co-prime
determine whether {num1} and {num2} share any factor other than 1
are {num1} and {num2} co-prime to each other
find if the pair {num1} and {num2} is safe in treasure game
verify co-primality of {num1} and {num2}

solution_steps.explain: Determine all positive divisors for both numbers.
If no factor other than 1 is common, the pair is co-prime.
Conclude whether the pair is co-prime based on whether 1 is the only shared divisor.

concepts.title: Product of Prime Factors
concepts.definition: Reconstructing an integer by multiplying together all elements of its prime factorisation.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying the prime building blocks in any order yields the original composite number.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: find the number whose prime factorisation is {factor1}, {factor2}, and {factor3}
calculate the number given prime factors {factor1}, {factor2}, {factor3}
what integer has prime factorisation {factor1} x {factor2} x {factor3}
determine the value of a number with prime factors {factor1}, {factor2}, {factor3}
multiply prime factors {factor1}, {factor2}, {factor3} to reconstruct the number

solution_steps.explain: Multiply factor1 by factor2 to get an intermediate product.
Multiply the intermediate product by factor3 to find the final number.
Confirm the product matches the original composite number by checking that all prime factors divide it exactly.

concepts.title: Divisibility Check via Prime Factorisation
concepts.definition: A number is divisible by another if all prime factors of the divisor appear in the prime factorisation of the dividend with equal or greater frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Divisibility holds if the dividend contains all prime components of the divisor.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: use prime factorisation to test if {dividend} is divisible by {divisor}
check if {divisor} divides {dividend} using prime factors
determine whether prime factors of {divisor} are included in {dividend}
is {dividend} divisible by {divisor} according to factor inclusion
verify if {divisor} is a factor of {dividend} via prime decomposition

solution_steps.explain: Express the dividend as a product of prime numbers.
Express the divisor as a product of prime numbers.
Verify if every prime factor of the divisor appears in the dividend with sufficient frequency.

concepts.title: Divisibility Rules for 2, 5, and 10
concepts.definition: Testing whether a number is divisible by 2, 5, or 10 by examining its final digit.
concepts.key_idea: The unit digit alone determines divisibility for powers/factors of 10.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: test if {num} is divisible by {divisor}
check divisibility of {num} by {divisor} using last digit rule
determine if {num} ends in a digit divisible by {divisor}
is {num} divisible by {divisor}
find whether {num} is a multiple of {divisor} without long division

solution_steps.explain: Observe the rightmost digit of the number.
Check if unit digit is in {0,2,4,6,8} for 2, in {0,5} for 5, or equal to 0 for 10.
Conclude whether the number is divisible by the divisor based on whether the unit digit satisfies the matching criterion.

concepts.title: Divisibility Rules for 4 and 8
concepts.definition: Testing divisibility by 4 or 8 by checking if the number formed by the last two or three digits is divisible by 4 or 8 respectively.
concepts.key_idea: Higher powers of 2 require examining a corresponding number of ending digits.
question_patterns: in Class 6 Prime Time: check if {num} is divisible by 4 using last two digits
test whether {num} is divisible by 8 using last three digits
determine if {num} is a multiple of 4 or 8 without full division
verify divisibility of {num} by 4
is {num} divisible by 8

solution_steps.explain: Form a sub-number from the last two digits (for 4) or last three digits (for 8).
Divide the extracted sub-number by 4 or 8 to determine overall divisibility.
If the sub-number divides evenly, the whole number is divisible by 4 or 8; otherwise it is not.
